messages:
Maya (support): glyphpay reporting sudden 429 spikes and increased latency on their dedicated pool since 03/22 02:00 UTC. customer says auth failures intermittently (token rejected) and lots of retries. attaching quick repro and logs.
Devon (oncall): looking. do we have tenant metrics for evictions / context length?
Maya (support): repro steps: 1) multi-turn conversations with ~30k token histories (longctx) 2) concurrent 50 rps 3) requests start getting 429s after ~8 minutes. sample log:```[2026-03-22T02:11:04Z] tenant=glyphpay kvcache.evicted=1274 kvcache.size_mb=312 kvcache.slab_frag_pct=18 mem.used_mb=4864 requests.429=12```
Lina (infra): that slab_frag_pct is alarming for that pool. eviction counts + slab fragmentation => allocator can't place new KV pages, causing request-level backpressure which surfaces as throttles. any pattern on sequence lengths?
Maya (support): yes, avg sequence_length ~ 18k tokens for those bursts.
Aaron (eng-runtime): long contexts + megabatch concurrency will amplify KV pressure. current dedicated config for glyphpay uses default kvcache.max_tenants = unlimited and slab_compaction interval = 30m. we recently saw heap drift in kernels after a compaction pass fails to reclaim fragmented slabs. quick mitigation: set kvcache.per_tenant_limit_mb=256 and reduce max_context_tokens to 12k for that pool. also bump burst capacity if possible.
Devon (oncall): putting a temporary per-tenant cap and lowering max_context is low-risk. I'll trigger limit rollout in the next 10m and monitor.
Jeff (billing): flagged a billing anomaly: glyphpay billed tokens jump ~3x during retry storms — looks like retries counted as new calls. recommend enabling dedup/idempotency for client and adjust billing window to exclude retried requests pending root cause.
OpsBot: deploy started: infra/limits/glyphpay-cap-2026-03-22 @devon.
Lina (infra): note: we have a pending infra patch that improves slab compaction (PR #4127) but it needs a canary. Suggest canary on a seed host before fleet rollout. compaction failure logs:```ERROR compactor: unable to consolidate slab slab_id=0x4f7 err=alloc_fragmentation_threshold_exceeded```
Aaron (eng-runtime): long-term fix: add adaptive kv eviction that prefers old prefix entries over recent short-lived KV windows for long-context workloads. we can also surface tenant-level kvcache metrics to the console so customers see their pressure and can self-tune.
Devon (oncall): current status: caps rolled to 256MB, max_context enforced at 12k for glyphpay, autoscale policy set to conservative (scale-up threshold 65% used -> faster). watching eviction rate and 429s.
Maya (support): customer notified of temporary limits and asked to test. they asked for repro assist if they see auth token rejections persist.
Aaron (eng-runtime): if auth rejections persist, capture auth proxy logs (X-Request-Id) and check if service is returning 503/504 upstream during backpressure — retries might lead to token expiry collisions. also recommend enabling short-lived session pinning to reduce token churn.
Jeff (billing): I'll create a billing credit ticket pending root-cause and capture token-retry deltas. ticket created: BILL-8429.
Lina (infra): canary for compactor scheduled in 30m. if stable, we'll roll to the rest of the dedicated pool overnight.
Devon (oncall): follow-ups: 1) confirm 429 drop in next 30m 2) gather kvcache.evicted, slab_frag_pct, mem.used_mb per-host 3) if no improvement, escalate to runtime eng for live debug. tagging @Aaron.
Maya (support): thanks team — keeping customer updated. will post results here. :thumbsup:
